canonical_rules: display text is the source of truth; where the PDF's segment guide wording differs, segments were corrected to tile the display text exactly (differences logged in errata)
straight ASCII apostrophes (') and quotes (") are canonical; the answer checker MUST normalize curly<->straight before comparing
internal whitespace normalized to single spaces; checker should collapse whitespace runs and trim before comparing
everything else is exact-match: spelling, word order, capitals, and punctuation all count
segments are the reveal/re-read chunks used during the writing phase; joined with single spaces they reproduce the display text exactly (validated programmatically)

errata.issue: Segment guide says 'The man said,' but the display sentence says 'The boy said,'. Canonical text follows the display ('The boy said,').
Segment guide says 'The puppy isn't' vs display 'That puppy isn't'. Canonical follows display.
Segment guide says 'That boy has some pets' vs display 'That kid has some pets'. Canonical follows display.
Segment guide says 'Something was in the way.' vs display 'Something was in its way.' Canonical follows display.
Segment guide includes 'still' ('Why were these birds still hungry') which the display sentence omits. Canonical follows display (no 'still').

'The man wanted someone to move that big rock out of the way?' is declarative but ends with a question mark, in both display and segments. Since the checker enforces exact punctuation, this trains a likely error.
errata.action: Confirm with Dr. Blank; expected fix is a period. Kept as printed in this file pending sign-off.

errata.issue: Segment guide ends 'babies big.' (period) vs display 'Are some babies big?' Canonical follows display ('?').
Segment guide says 'in that truck now' vs display 'in the truck now'. Canonical follows display.
Segment guide places the question mark outside the closing quote (there"?) while display places it inside (there?"). Canonical follows display.

skills_assessment.purpose: Placement test for children NOT already placed via the reading program (source pp. 92-95). Dictation: adult/app reads each sentence aloud; child writes it without seeing it; no guidance during the test.
scoring_rules: A word is correct only if it contains no errors: no omitted letters, no added letters, no misplaced letters.
Each word counts at most one error (e.g., 'rocket' written 'rokit' = 1 error).
Capitals and punctuation are scored as separate units, per the table.
Score per level = correct words + correct capitals + correct punctuation.
flow: Administer Level 1 set; score it (child takes a short break).
If score >= criterion: advance to the next level's set.
If score < criterion: STOP. Placement = the level of the set just failed (pass L1, fail L2 -> start program at Level 2).
If the child passes Level 5: skills exceed Memory Master; offer maintenance mode or exit.
Usually one sitting with breaks; may be split over two sessions.
